skill.name: making-commits
skill.description: Guidelines for creating clear, maintainable git commits during larger coding tasks.
skill.summary: Guides AI assistants to make small, focused git commits with linting and formatting checks.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in this prompt-only skill. Manual review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable code, network access, or filesystem instructions beyond normal git workflow guidance.

content.value_statement: Large changes can produce unclear commit history that is hard to review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to make small, tested commits.
actual_capabilities: Encourages small commits that address one concern or feature.
Guides assistants to split large changes into logical separate commits.
Promotes clear and maintainable commit history for bigger tasks.
Reminds assistants to run linting before committing.
Reminds assistants to run formatting before committing.
limitations: Does not provide git command syntax or automation scripts.
Does not define a commit message format.
Does not run linting or formatting by itself.
Does not cover branching, pull requests, or release workflows.

use_cases.title: Maintain Reviewable Feature Work
use_cases.description: A developer uses the skill to keep a multi-file feature split into small, focused commits.

use_cases.title: Prepare Cleaner Assistant Commits
use_cases.description: An engineering lead uses the skill to guide AI assistants toward easier review and rollback.

use_cases.title: Standardize Larger Task Hygiene
use_cases.description: A team member uses the skill to remind assistants to lint and format before committing work.

prompt_templates.title: Make One Focused Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple completed change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current changes and make one small git commit for the completed concern. Run formatting and linting before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Split a Larger Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for grouped commits after a broad task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the working tree and divide the changes into logical commits. Each commit should address one feature, fix, or cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Reviewable History
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before opening a review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize the current work into a clear commit history for review. Separate unrelated concerns and verify linting and formatting first.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Commit Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request when changes may be incomplete or mixed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether the current changes are ready to commit. Identify logical commit groups, missing checks, and any work that should stay unstaged.

output_examples.input: The assistant finished a feature and several cleanup edits in one working tree.
output: Suggests separating the feature work from cleanup changes.
Runs linting and formatting before committing.
Creates commits that each describe one completed concern.

output_examples.input: The assistant is about to commit a large refactor.
output: Reviews the changed files for logical boundaries.
Splits independent refactor steps into smaller commits.
Leaves unrelated or unfinished work out of the commit.

best_practices: Use the skill after a task has enough complete work to commit.
Review the proposed commit grouping before allowing commits.
Keep linting and formatting commands aligned with the project setup.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated features, fixes, and cleanup in one commit.
Do not commit before formatting and linting have run successfully.
Do not use the skill as a replacement for branch or release policy.

faq.question: Does this skill execute git commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for AI assistants. The assistant still decides which commands to run in the active environment.

faq.question: Can it create commit messages?
faq.answer: It can guide focused commits, but the source skill does not define a commit message template.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed skill is prompt-only and contains no network instructions or executable code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large coding tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is intended for bigger tasks where clear and maintainable commit history matters.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It specifically mentions linting and formatting, not test execution.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
